newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Moslems defy Israel to pray at Jerusalem shrine.
newsitem.headline: Moslems defy Israel to pray at Jerusalem shrine.

text.p: Jumping over walls and trekking across muddy fields, hundreds of Palestinians defied an Israeli ban on entry to Jerusalem to attend Friday prayers at al-Aqsa mosque in the holy month of Ramadan, witnesses said.

They said minor scuffles broke out as Israeli soldiers tried to hold back Palestinians who jammed military checkpoints around Jerusalem. Israel deployed more than 3,000 policemen in the city in expectation of an influx of worshippers.
Israel Radio estimated 200,000 people attended the prayers.

Some Palestinians broke through army lines while others jumped over walls and circumvented the military roadblocks by walking across muddied fields. Israeli soldiers gave chase to Palestinians but many got through, the witnesses said.
Israel has barred Palestinian from the West Bank and Gaza Strip from entering the holy city without special permits for almost three years in an attempt to stem Arab-Israeli violence.
Some 200,000 Palestinians entered Jerusalem every day before the closure for worship, medical treatment or work.

In the West Bank town of Hebron scuffles broke out between Israeli soldiers and Moslem worshippers at the gates of al-Ibrahimi mosque, where thousands of Palestinians tried to attend Friday prayers, witnesses said.

The mosque, at the burial site of the biblical Abraham also revered by Jews, remained under Israel control after the Jewish state handed 80 percent of the town to the Palestinians on January 17 under a self-rule deal.

Witnesses said Israeli police beat a Palestinian youth and detained him while he was trying to force his way into the heavily guarded shrine. Many people were forced to pray in the open courtyard after they were unable to get in.
